tagline: From a gold town to a silver ghost, by the old rail grade.
intro: The byway comes into Hillsboro on NM 152 and turns south on NM 27 along the eastern flank of the Black Range, through Chihuahuan grassland, to Lake Valley and on to Nutt. NM 27 stayed graded or gravel until it was paved sometime in the 1960s.
Below Lake Valley the road keeps beside the grade of a Santa Fe spur built in 1884 to carry supplies in and ore out. The tracks came up in 1934. The grade is still there to see.

moments.title: Hillsboro
moments.text: Two prospectors picked up loose rock here in 1877 that assayed at $160 a ton, and the town that followed was the county seat until 1936.

moments.title: Lake Valley
moments.text: Miners here broke into a silver-lined cavity they named the bridal chamber, good for 2.5 million ounces, and the last resident left in 1994.

moments.title: Nutt
moments.text: Nutt calls itself the Middle of Nowhere, and its one claim to fame is the 1892 payroll train that Black Jack Ketchum's gang held up just outside town.

practical: The Bureau of Land Management restricts access to the old buildings at Lake Valley to daylight hours.
